description:
FOUND s494p (Opus, 2026-09-25), member 1 (iii) of perf round 35 (#2098): the shapes table's `while ($i++ < N) { $s .= "ab" }` row was thought to be a LOOP-spelling decline.  It is not — PCL_B_DEBUG on scratch/s494p/s1a.pl:
    my ($s3, $i) = ("", 0); while ($i++ < $_[0]) { $s3 .= "ab" }   -> $s3 unboxable=0 strbuf=0 reasons=[write-list]
    my $s4 = ""; my $i = 0;  while ($i++ < $_[0]) { $s4 .= "ab" }   -> $s4 unboxable=1 strbuf=1
The while loop licenses exactly like a foreach block; the decline is the LIST declaration: every `$scalar` inside a list LHS is written by the p-list-= box machinery (D11), which cannot store into a raw slot.  That is an EMISSION-ROUTE condition, not a statement about the variable.
FIX SHAPE (measure first): normalise `my (A, B, …) = (X, Y, …);` into per-variable declarations when both sides have the same arity, every LHS is a plain scalar, and every RHS element is a LITERAL (number / non-interpolating string / undef) — the literal restriction is what makes it exact: with a non-literal RHS the split would let a later RHS element see an earlier NEW variable (`my ($a, $b) = (1, $a)` reads the OUTER $a).  Where: the one place the declaration statement is read (Parser2's Statement::Variable lowering + the VarAnnotator decl walk must agree — one predicate, as append_rest is for #2098).  BAR: corpus-diff explained per class, the shapes row linear, `PCL_OPT=none` runs identically, sweep.

=== DONE (s501q) ===
SHIPPED as Kind-A `list-decl-split`: Parser2::_split_literal_list_decls lowers `my ($a, $b) = (L1, L2);` as its declarations apart when every LHS is a plain distinct scalar, the counts are equal, every RHS element is a LITERAL (number / non-interpolating string / undef) and the statement is not its block's last (so a value/count is never asked of it).  The literal rule is what makes it exact (`my ($a, $b) = (1, $a)` is untouched).
SIZING: `while ($i++ < 200k) { $s .= "ab" }` with the list declaration 29.07 s -> 0.033 s (the split spelling) -- quadratic -> linear (load 7.4, a LOADED reading, but the ratio is a complexity class).  MEASURED on the tree: the shapes row 30.27 s -> 0.039 s; bench `listdeclcat` -51.9 %.  Final-tree numbers: FINAL TREE (s503, 71bd29ef on main 2284d58d, quiet box load 0.8-1.7, bench-exec BENCH_K=5 two interleaved passes vs base-2284d58d, scratch/s501q/bench-final/table.txt): sigarith 0.1163 -> 0.0235 s (-79.8 %, 0.22x of perl), passarr 0.2683 -> 0.1683 (-37.3 %), listdeclcat 0.4491 -> 0.2213 (-50.7 %), lcbytes 0.1534 -> 0.1422 (-7.3 %; 209e7533 0.1134), ucshort 0.1074 -> 0.1077 (+0.3 %, ctl +1.2 %; 209e7533 0.1046), methret +2.0 % (rerun -2.1 %); real programs (realprog-final.txt, K=5): Air-mass 1.303 -> 0.979 s (-24.9 %), Perfect-shuffle 0.620 -> 0.437 (-29.6 %), Sub-unit-squares 0.425 -> 0.327 (-22.9 %), ctl <= 0.4 %; compile time +0.4 % wall over 111 files.  FLAGGED: fibret +4.3..5.4 % in bench-exec (direct timing +0.6..2.6 %; an identity parameter copy is not faster, so not #2570 -- cause not found)..
PROBES: r501q-listdecl 34/34 perl; b2114.pl == base.  corpus-diff class list-decl-split: aassign hash loopctl lop multideref recurse sort sprintf2 (+ signatures).  A stale guard (parser2-01 'my (LIST) init via p-list-=') re-pointed at a non-literal element at the s502 rebase.
subject: PERF (quadratic `.=`): a LIST declaration `my ($s, $i) = ("", 0);` boxes $s (VarAnnotator reason `write-list`, D11), so the str-buffer licence never applies and `while ($i++ < $n) { $s .= "ab" }` stays quadratic (200k appends 28 s) — the separate `my $s = ""; my $i = 0;` spelling is linear
